text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Senate to debate draft on wine law.
- Tarom SA state-run airline to increase tariffs for doemstic flights starting January 16.
- The dollar fetches over 6,000 lei at retail shops.
- State-run Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare launches new Prima debit card.
- Romania to increase price of locally-produced crude oil to $105 a tonne, up from $102, the paper says.
- Some 5,000 Romanian pensioners wait for the government to take steps to cushion effects of recent price increases.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- World Bank is wiling to support Romania's economic reforms, the paper says.
- The Romanian Oil Company needs $1.4 billion for crude oil imports in 1997.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The upper Senate plans to move headquarters into the Palace of Parliament built by ex-Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu. The Chamber of Deputies is already based there.
- Former political prisoner Octavian Radulescu pressed charges in court against ex-President Ion Iliescu for instigating to violence during riots led by coalminers in 1990.
- Senate appointed commission to control activity of State Ownership Fund and the five Private Ownership Funds, recently turned into investment trusts.

- Romania and Poland are not competitors but partners which support each other's integration in NATO and EU, President Emil Constantinescu and Aleksander Kwasniewski said during Constantinescu's official visit to Warsaw on Monday.
ADEVARUL
- Founder of troubled private Dacia Felix SA bank, former tennis player Sever Muresan, has started to sell his properties, the newspaper says.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Hospitals affecetd by shortage of funds after recent increases in petrol prices.
- Prosecutors issued two arrest warrants against union leader Miron Cozma in 1993 for allegedly undermining state authority, but police failed to act accordingly.
LIBERTATEA
- Last Sunday's lottery draw offered prizes totalling 11.6 billion lei. More than 10 million Romanians bought tickets for the lottery.
- Newspaper rewarded with one million lei the prosecutor who ordered the arrest of coal miners' leader Miron Cosma.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Three Romanians won highest lottery prizes ever worth some 1.17 billion lei each. ($= 4,363 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
